title: Stop requiring a full cargo test run from the producer
summary: The producer prompt tells producers to run the full `cargo test --locked`, and run.rs sends a report back (once) without a real result for it. Remove both, tell producers to run targeted tests, and keep the post-producer fmt, clippy and full-suite checks that Athena runs on the candidate. The audience is Athena operators and producers, who lose 9 to 11 minutes per full run.

defaults_applied.how: Lifecycle and job_plan tests are updated for the new behavior; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
The demand is removed in both the prompt and the run.rs enforcement, not only the wording of one.
A criterion runs the lifecycle tests and checks that no send-back happens and that failing candidates are still rejected.
The full-suite gate stays enforced by Athena's own post-producer check.
The decision and CHANGELOG text states the reason and the measured run times.
One focused change to the producer test requirement.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Athena already runs fmt, clippy and the full test suite on the candidate and a failure fails it, as the request states; I did not trace that code path in full.
The send-back mechanism for unmet acceptance criteria stays; only the full-test demand is removed.
Pinned study jobs were already exempt, so their behavior is unchanged.
A new decision entry (next free number after the highest in docs/decisions.md) is appropriate because this reverses part of D95; D95 itself is not rewritten.
The producer may still report a full-suite run if it chooses to; the report schema keeps checks_run.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md no longer tells the producer to run the full `cargo test --locked` or to report it. It says to run targeted tests (`cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`) while working and that Athena runs fmt, clippy and the full suite on the candidate.

In crates/athena-core/src/run.rs the producer loop no longer sends a report back for lacking a real full `cargo test --locked` result. The `ran_full_tests` and `tests_missing` gating and the sent-back test text are removed. The send-back for unmet acceptance criteria is kept.

The checks Athena runs on the candidate (fmt, clippy, full test) and their effect on the final verdict are unchanged. A failing check still fails the candidate. The producer-report-gaps note to the verifier no longer tells it to run the full suite, and the verifier prompt still says to cite recorded results.

Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`. The tests show that a producer report with no full-suite check, or with `not-run`, goes to the verifier without a send-back. A report with unmet criteria is still sent back once. A candidate whose recorded test check fails is still rejected.
Run `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean, with no unused-code warnings left by the removed gating.

docs/decisions.md records the change as a new decision that amends D95 and its D95 follow-up wording, and docs/design/athena-v0.md and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] no longer say the producer must run the full suite. The documents state the reason with the figures from the two jobs (nvbb: six runs, 1800 s deadline; 9 to 11 minutes per run).

out_of_scope: Changing verifier behavior or its prompt beyond the gaps note
Changing which checks Athena runs on the candidate
Changing the send-back for unmet acceptance criteria
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: run.rs plus several lifecycle tests change, and the verifier cites a cold full-suite record of 9 to 11 minutes.
